title: Three letters, then a pause before the wisdom begins.
subtitle: Opening letters whose meaning Allah knows
then: Surah Luqman came in Makkah, when people were being pulled back to the creed of their forefathers. It opens with three letters whose meaning is {idea}known to Allah alone{/idea}. They catch the ear before the message starts.
now: You open the app between notifications, thumb still itching to scroll. Three letters you cannot translate. {idea}That is the cue to slow down.{/idea} The words after them deserve your full attention, not your leftover attention.
old: If I cannot explain something, I skip past it.
new: Some things are there to make me stop and listen before I speak.
try: Before your next recitation, put the phone face down and take one slow breath first.

title: This Book is wise, and it makes you wise.
subtitle: The Book is called wise from the first line
then: The surah is named after Luqman, a wise man the Arabs already quoted in their sayings and poems. Before his story, Allah calls the Qur'an itself {idea}the wise Book{/idea}. The wisdom people admired in Luqman is here in full.
now: You save quotes from podcasts and screenshots of life advice. You ask friends what to do about the job offer. {idea}The wisest voice is already on your shelf{/idea}, and it is rarely the one you open first.
old: Wisdom is something I collect from clever people online.
new: The deepest wisdom I can find is in the Book I already have.
try: Next time you face a choice today, read one page of Qur'an before asking anyone else.

title: Guidance and mercy, opened for those who do good.
subtitle: Who the Book helps most
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah made the Qur'an {reward}guidance, healing and mercy{/reward} for the Muhsinin. These are people who do good, keep ties with family, and do not do it to be seen or thanked.
now: You help your mother with her forms and nobody posts about it. You cover a shift for a tired colleague. {idea}That quiet goodness is what opens the Book to you.{/idea} The verses start to feel written for your day.
old: The Qur'an speaks to scholars, not to someone like me.
new: Doing good quietly is what makes the Book open up to me.
try: Do one kind thing today that no one will ever know about.

title: Prayer, giving, and certainty about what comes next.
subtitle: Three marks of the people who do good
then: Ibn Kathir describes them: they pray the obligatory prayers properly and on time, then add more. They pay zakah to those who deserve it. {idea}They are certain of the Hereafter{/idea}, so they do not look for thanks from people.
now: Payday comes and the money is already spoken for. Rent, bills, the car. {reward}Giving first{/reward} feels like a stretch. So does stopping for prayer during a busy afternoon. Certainty about tomorrow is what makes both feel possible.
old: I will give and pray more once life calms down.
new: Being sure of what comes after is what makes prayer and giving feel natural now.
try: Pray your next prayer within ten minutes of its time starting.

title: They are on guidance, and they are the successful.
subtitle: What success means in this surah
then: Ibn Kathir explains that these people follow Allah's guidance with clear understanding. They are {reward}successful in this world and in the Hereafter{/reward}. The Makkans measured success by wealth and tribe. This verse gives a different measure.
now: The school reunion where everyone compares jobs and houses. The LinkedIn post about a promotion. {idea}Success here has a different definition{/idea}: being on guidance from your Lord, and staying there.
old: Success is what people can see on my profile.
new: Success is being guided by my Lord, in this life and the next.
try: Write your own one-line definition of success, and check it against this verse.

title: Some people buy noise to drown out guidance.
subtitle: Idle talk used to pull people away
then: Ibn Kathir contrasts those who soften to the Qur'an with those who turn to idle talk instead. Qatadah said a person may not even pay money for it. {trap}Buying it means loving it{/trap}, and the more misguided he is, the more he prefers it over what benefits him.
now: Autoplay starts the next episode before you decide. The clips, the gossip channels, the endless commentary. {trap}Hours go in and nothing comes out.{/trap} Notice what you keep choosing over the Qur'an, and how easily.
old: What I watch and listen to does not really affect me.
new: What I keep choosing to hear slowly shapes what I can still hear.
try: Turn off autoplay on one app today.

title: He turns away as if his ears were blocked.
subtitle: Pride that refuses to hear
then: Ibn Kathir says the person fond of idle play turns away when the verses are recited. {trap}It annoys him to hear them{/trap}, because he has no interest in them. The verse warns that his punishment will hurt him as listening hurt him.
now: Someone in the family group chat shares a short reminder. You feel the eye-roll before you read it. {trap}The mute button is right there.{/trap} The question is not what they sent, but why it irritates you so fast.
old: I just do not like being preached at.
new: Sometimes the irritation is pride, and the reminder was for me.
try: Read the next reminder someone sends you to the end, slowly, before reacting.

title: Faith and good deeds open Gardens of Delight.
subtitle: The other path, right after the warning
then: Right after the one who turns away, Allah describes those who {idea}believe and do righteous deeds{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says the Gardens hold delights that have {reward}never crossed the mind of any human being{/reward}.
now: You picture the best day you ever had: the wedding, the trip, the evening with everyone laughing. {reward}It is not even close.{/reward} What reaches it is ordinary: believing, and then doing the next good thing.
old: Paradise is too far away to think about on a Tuesday.
new: Every small good deed on an ordinary day is a step toward it.
try: Pair one belief with one action today, such as thanking Allah and then thanking a person.

title: Forever, because Allah never breaks a promise.
subtitle: Why the reward is certain
then: Ibn Kathir says the people of the Garden stay forever, {reward}never leaving and never wanting change{/reward}. It will surely happen, because Allah never breaks His promise and is able to do all things.
now: The landlord who said he would fix it. The boss who promised a raise next quarter. You have learned to discount promises. {idea}This one is different{/idea}: the One making it is able, and never lets a promise slip.
old: Promises get broken, so I do not lean on them.
new: Allah's promise is the one I can lean my whole weight on.
try: Keep one small promise you made to someone this week, today.

title: Sky without pillars, steady mountains, rain and growing life.
subtitle: Signs of the Creator and Provider all around you
then: Ibn Kathir says the heavens have {idea}no pillars, visible or invisible{/idea}. He notes that when Allah reminds us He is the Creator, He also reminds us He is the Provider. The Makkans were asked to look with open eyes at what was around them.
now: The commute home under a wide evening sky. The rain on the bus window. The fruit stall on the corner, every colour there. {idea}You walk past a hundred signs a day{/idea} with your eyes on a screen.
old: The sky and rain are just background to my day.
new: Everything around me is made and provided, and it points to Him.
try: Step outside once today and look up at the sky for a full minute.

title: This is His creation. Show Me what others made.
subtitle: A challenge to everything people rely on besides Allah
then: Ibn Kathir says all this creation comes from {idea}Allah's power alone, with no partner{/idea}. The idol worshippers of Makkah were challenged: show what your idols created. Their error was plain, not hidden.
now: Your confidence rests on the job, the savings, the right connection. Ask honestly: {trap}what did any of them create?{/trap} They are gifts that were made and given. The Maker deserves the trust.
old: My security comes from what I have built up.
new: Nothing I lean on made itself. Only the Maker deserves my trust.
try: Name one thing you lean on too much, and thank Allah for giving it to you.

title: Luqman was given wisdom, and it began with thanks.
subtitle: Gratitude is the first thing wisdom teaches
then: Most scholars held that Luqman was a righteous servant, not a prophet. A story says his master asked for the best and worst parts of a sheep, and both times he brought {idea}the tongue and the heart{/idea}. Allah's first command to him in this verse was to give thanks.
now: The hot shower, the working phone, the friend who still texts back. You complain fast and thank slowly. {reward}Thanks returns to you{/reward}: a calmer heart and eyes that notice more. Allah loses nothing if you forget.
old: Gratitude is something I owe, like a bill.
new: Gratitude is a gift to myself. Allah needs nothing from me.
try: Before bed, name three things from today you are grateful for.

title: A father's first advice: never set anyone beside Allah.
subtitle: What Luqman gave his son first
then: Ibn Kathir says Luqman advised the person {idea}closest and most beloved to him{/idea}, so he gave him the best he knew. He started with worshipping Allah alone. When Companions worried about a verse on wrongdoing, the Prophet ﷺ pointed them to {trap}this exact line about shirk{/trap}.
now: Your child is about to leave for university, or start a first job. You have one car ride to say what matters. Grades, money, be careful. {idea}Luqman's list started somewhere else.{/idea}
old: The most important things to teach my children are practical skills.
new: The first thing worth passing on is who to worship.
try: Tell a younger person in your family, in your own words, why you worship Allah alone.

title: She carried you in weakness upon weakness. Thank her too.
subtitle: Gratitude to Allah, then to parents
then: Ibn Kathir notes that worshipping Allah and honouring parents {idea}often come together in the Qur'an{/idea}. Here the mother is singled out: tired, stressed, up with the child night and day. The verse reminds the child of her care.
now: Your mum calls during your lunch break and you let it ring. She asks the same question twice. {reward}Once she stayed up every night with you{/reward}, and never let it ring. Allah put thanking her right next to thanking Him.
old: My parents did what parents are supposed to do.
new: What my mother carried for me deserves thanks next to my thanks to Allah.
try: Call your mother, or make dua for her if she has passed, and say thank you for one specific thing.

title: Do not obey them in shirk, but stay kind to them.
subtitle: Firm in faith, gentle with family
then: Sa'd bin Malik said this verse came about him. His mother refused to eat until he gave up Islam. {idea}He would not give it up{/idea}, and she ate. The surah introduction says young converts were told: parents have high rights, but {trap}not when they pull you to shirk{/trap}.
now: A family dinner where your choice is mocked again. You feel two pulls: give in, or walk out and stop calling. {idea}The verse holds both lines{/idea}: do not give up your faith, and keep showing up with kindness.
old: If my family opposes my faith, I either give in or walk away.
new: I can stay firm on Allah and still be gentle with them.
try: Do one kind thing for a relative you disagree with, without bringing up the disagreement.

title: A mustard seed hidden in rock, and Allah still brings it.
subtitle: Nothing small escapes Him
then: Ibn Kathir says Luqman taught his son that even a deed the size of a mustard seed {idea}will be brought out on the Day{/idea} and weighed. Allah is aware of {idea}an ant's footsteps in the darkest night{/idea}.
now: The small lie on a form. The tip you quietly left extra. The sharp comment you deleted before sending. {idea}None of it is lost.{/idea} That is a warning, and also a comfort for the good no one noticed.
old: Small things do not count. Only big deeds matter.
new: Every small deed is seen and kept, good and bad.
try: Do one tiny good deed today on purpose, knowing Allah sees it.

title: Pray, call to good, and expect to need patience.
subtitle: Luqman's advice for living it out

key.label: Why patience is in the list

then: Ibn Kathir says Luqman knew that anyone who calls to good and forbids wrong {trap}will meet harm and annoyance from people{/trap}. So he paired it with patience, calling it one of the most important commands.
now: You speak up in the office about a dodgy expense claim. Now the room is cold when you walk in. {reward}Luqman expected that.{/reward} Patience was never an extra. It was part of the plan.
old: If doing right brings trouble, maybe I did it wrong.
new: Trouble after doing right is expected, and patience is part of the deed.
try: Think of one situation where you spoke up and it cost you. Make dua for patience about it.

title: Do not turn your cheek from people or walk proudly.
subtitle: Arrogance shows in the face and the walk
then: Ibn Kathir explains: do not turn your face away when people speak to you, {trap}looking down on them{/trap}. Be gentle and {idea}greet them with a cheerful face{/idea}. Allah does not like the one who admires himself.
now: The cleaner says good morning and you nod without looking up from your phone. The junior colleague asks a question and you answer to your screen. {idea}Turn your face to them.{/idea} Small, and it changes the whole exchange.
old: I am just busy, not arrogant.
new: How I turn my face to people shows what my heart thinks of them.
try: Today, look up and smile at one person you usually rush past.

title: Walk at a moderate pace, and lower your voice.
subtitle: The closing advice of Luqman
then: Ibn Kathir says this means walking {idea}neither slow and lazy nor too fast{/idea}, and not raising your voice without need. Mujahid said a raised voice was likened to {trap}a donkey's braying{/trap} for its loudness.
now: The argument in the car park. The family debate where the loudest uncle always wins. {idea}Volume is not the same as being right.{/idea} The calmer voice is often the one people remember.
old: If I do not raise my voice, no one will take me seriously.
new: A calm, low voice carries more dignity than a loud one.
try: In your next disagreement, deliberately speak more quietly than the other person.

title: Everything is put at your service. Still some argue.
subtitle: Favours seen and unseen
then: Ibn Kathir lists the stars, rain, rivers, crops and fruits, and also {reward}the hidden favours: Messengers and Books{/reward} that remove doubts. Yet some still dispute about Allah {trap}without knowledge or proof{/trap}.
now: The phone in your hand runs on materials from the earth. The water from your tap came down as rain. {reward}The reminder that reached you today is a hidden favour too.{/reward} Arguing comes easily. Noticing takes a pause.
old: I have questions, so I can wave the whole thing away.
new: The favours around me are evidence too, if I stop to count them.
try: List five favours you used today without thinking, including one that is not physical.

title: We follow our fathers, even if the path leads to fire?
subtitle: Habit is not proof

row.title: it is what we always did

then: The surah introduction says the Makkans were invited to {idea}give up blind imitation of their forefathers{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says they had {trap}no proof except that their fathers did it{/trap}, even if Shaytan was calling them to the Fire.
now: Wedding customs, money habits, the way your family talks about other people. Some of it is good. {trap}Some of it you never questioned.{/trap} We always did it this way is a reason to look closer, not to stop looking.
old: If my family has always done it, it must be fine.
new: Habits I inherited still need checking against what Allah sent.
try: Pick one family habit and ask yourself honestly whether it pleases Allah.

title: Submit your face to Allah and hold the firmest handhold.
subtitle: Sincere surrender plus doing good
then: Ibn Kathir says submitting your face means {idea}doing deeds sincerely for His sake{/idea} and following His law. The one who does this and does good {reward}has a firm promise from Allah{/reward}.
now: The redundancy email. The test results you are waiting on. Everything you were holding feels loose. {reward}There is one handhold that does not break{/reward}: turning your whole self to Allah and doing the next good thing.
old: I feel safe when I am in control of things.
new: I am safe when I am holding on to Allah, whatever else slips.
try: When you feel anxious today, stop and say: to Allah all matters return.

title: Do not let their rejection eat you up.
subtitle: Comfort for the one whose message is refused
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah told the Prophet ﷺ {idea}not to grieve over those who disbelieve{/idea}. Their return is to Allah, who will tell them what they did. {idea}Nothing in their hearts is hidden from Him.{/idea}
now: You keep sending your brother reminders and he leaves them on read. You lie awake replaying the last argument. {idea}Your part is to be sincere and kind.{/idea} Where his heart goes is between him and Allah.
old: If someone I love rejects the truth, it is my failure.
new: I carry the message with care. The hearts belong to Allah.
try: Make dua for one person you worry about, then let the worry rest with Allah tonight.

title: Enjoyment for a little while, then a heavy outcome.
subtitle: The short shelf life of comfort without faith
then: Ibn Kathir says this enjoyment is {reward}in this world{/reward}, and it is brief. After it comes a punishment that is hard to bear. He links it to 10:69-70, where {trap}worldly enjoyment is followed by the return to Allah{/trap}.
now: The weekend that flew by. The holiday that ended before you unpacked. {idea}A whole life feels like that at the end.{/idea} The question is not whether you enjoy it, but what you send ahead while you do.
old: I have plenty of time to sort out my priorities later.
new: This life is a little while, so what I do with it matters now.
try: Look at how you spent yesterday's free hour, and give one hour this week to something lasting.

title: They admit Allah created everything, then live as if not.
subtitle: Knowing the Creator is not the same as living by it

row.title: I believe, so I am fine

then: Ibn Kathir says the Makkan idol worshippers {idea}admitted that Allah alone created heaven and earth{/idea}. Yet they still worshipped things they knew He had created. {trap}Their own answer was the proof against them.{/trap}
now: Ask yourself who provides, and you answer Allah instantly. Then payday comes and the fear is about the boss, the market, the bonus. {trap}The answer is right, but the heart lives by another.{/trap}
old: I know Allah is the Creator, so my faith is sorted.
new: Knowing He created everything should change who I fear and hope in.
try: When you worry about money today, say Alhamdulillah and remind yourself who provides.

title: Everything belongs to Him, and He needs nothing.
subtitle: Al-Ghani, the Praiseworthy
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}He has no need of anyone or anything{/idea}, and everything else is in need of Him. He is praised for all that He creates and decrees, in every affair.
now: Your name is on the lease. Your phone, your car, your account. It feels like yours. {idea}Everything you hold is on loan{/idea} from the One who needs none of it, and gave it anyway.
old: What I worked for is simply mine.
new: All I have belongs to Allah, who needs nothing and still gives.
try: Give away one thing you own today that someone else needs more than you.

title: Every tree a pen, every sea ink, and still not enough.
subtitle: The Words of Allah have no end
then: Ibn Kathir says the number seven means {idea}a large amount, not a literal count{/idea}. The pens would break and the ink run dry. The Prophet ﷺ said in his prayer: {idea}I cannot praise You enough.{/idea}
now: You have a cloud full of notes, a library app, a search engine. It feels like everything can be known. {idea}Stand by the sea for a minute{/idea} and picture it as ink. Then picture it running dry.
old: I already understand most of what there is to know about Allah.
new: What I know of Allah is a drop. His Words never run out.
try: Learn the meaning of one Name of Allah you did not know well, today.

title: Raising all of humanity is as easy as raising one.
subtitle: Creation and resurrection are one command
then: Ibn Kathir says creating and resurrecting all of mankind is, to Allah's power, {idea}like creating one soul{/idea}. He hears all they say and sees all they do, {idea}as if hearing and seeing a single person{/idea}.
now: A crowded train at rush hour. Thousands of faces, and you feel like no one. {idea}To Allah you are not lost in the crowd.{/idea} He hears you as clearly as if you were the only one speaking.
old: With so many people, Allah cannot really notice me.
new: He hears and sees me as fully as if I were the only one.
try: In your next dua, speak to Allah about one small personal thing you thought too minor.

title: Night slides into day, and the sun keeps its course.
subtitle: The steady order of time
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah takes from the night and adds to the day, {idea}as in summer, then the reverse in winter{/idea}. The sun and moon each run to an appointed term. He ends with: Allah is aware of what you do.
now: The clocks change and your prayer times shift. Maghrib creeps later through spring. {idea}The same precision runs your day{/idea}, and the same Lord is aware of what you do with it.
old: Sunrise and sunset are just times on a weather app.
new: Each shift of light is a sign of an exact Lord who sees my day.
try: Watch the sunset tonight, or check the time of Maghrib and pray it on time.

title: Allah is the Truth. Everything else called on is false.
subtitle: Why the signs are shown

row.title: Allah
sub: the Truth, Most High, Most Great

then: Ibn Kathir says He shows His signs {idea}so you may know He is the Truth{/idea}. Nothing could move an atom's weight without His permission. {trap}If everyone came together, they could not create a fly.{/trap}
now: The horoscope app, the lucky number, the influencer you treat like a guide. {trap}None of them can move an atom.{/trap} The One who runs the sun and the moon is the One worth calling on.
old: A bit of superstition or reliance on people is harmless.
new: Only Allah is real power. Everything else depends on Him.
try: Delete or mute one thing you check for reassurance that is not Allah.

title: Ships float by His favour, a sign for the patient and grateful.
subtitle: Patience in hardship, thanks in ease
then: Ibn Kathir says that if Allah did not {idea}give the water the strength to carry ships{/idea}, they would not sail. The signs are for {reward}one who bears hardship with patience and gives thanks in ease{/reward}.
now: The ferry, the cargo ship that brought your shoes, the flight over the ocean. You take it as engineering. {idea}It is also a favour.{/idea} The patient and grateful are the ones who notice.
old: Things work because of science, not because of a favour.
new: The laws that make things work are His favour too.
try: Next time you travel, say a dua of thanks as you set off.

title: Sincere in the storm, half-hearted back on land.
subtitle: Calling on Allah only when waves rise
then: Ibn Kathir says when waves covered them like mountains or clouds, {idea}they called on Allah alone{/idea}. Safe on land, some held back. He explains Khattar as one who {trap}breaks his promise{/trap}, and Kafur as one who forgets blessings.
now: The hospital corridor at 3am. You promise Allah you will change everything. The scan comes back clear, and a month later the promise is gone. {idea}Remember the corridor.{/idea}
old: I turn to Allah when things get serious.
new: The dua I made in the storm is a promise to keep in the calm.
try: Recall one promise you made to Allah in a hard moment, and do one part of it today.

title: A Day when no father can help his son.
subtitle: Do not be fooled by this life or the Deceiver
then: Ibn Kathir says even if a father offered himself for his son, {trap}it would not be accepted{/trap}. Do not let contentment with this life make you forget the Hereafter, and do not let {trap}Shaytan's empty promises{/trap} deceive you about Allah.
now: You tell yourself your parents prayed enough for the family. Or that your kids will sort out your dua later. {idea}On that Day each person stands alone.{/idea} Today is still yours to prepare for it.
old: My family's goodness will somehow cover me.
new: No one can carry me on that Day, so I prepare my own way now.
try: Pick one good habit you have left to others in your family, and do it yourself today.

title: Five things only Allah knows, including your tomorrow.
subtitle: The keys of the Unseen
then: The Prophet ﷺ called these {idea}the five keys of the Unseen{/idea} that no one knows but Allah. Qatadah said: you do not know, son of Adam, {trap}when you will die{/trap}. You might die tomorrow.
now: Your calendar has next month's meetings and a holiday booked. The pension forecast runs thirty years ahead. {idea}None of it is promised.{/idea} Plan, and also live today as if it counts.
old: I know roughly how my life will go.
new: Tomorrow is with Allah. Today is the part I am given.
try: Do one thing today you have been putting off for later, such as a call, an apology, or a charity.
